title: To amend title 49, United States Code, with respect to certain grant assurances, and for other purposes.
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The expanded summary of the House passed version is repeated here.)

(Sec. 1) This bill declares that an airport owner or operator who renews a covered lease shall not be treated as violating that owner's or operator's written airport improvement project grant assurance requirement to maintain a schedule of airport passenger user charges that will make the airport as self-sustaining as possible under existing circumstances.

The bill defines "covered lease" to mean a lease:

  • already existing before enactment of this bill,
  • in which a nominal lease rate is provided,
  • under which the lessee is a federal or state government entity, and
  • that supports the operation of Air Force or Air National Guard aircraft at the airport or remotely from the airport.

summary.headline: This law says airport owners who renew certain low-rent leases with military aircraft operators will not be treated as breaking a federal grant rule on passenger charges.
summary.what_it_does: Airports that accept federal airport improvement grants promise to set passenger user charges so the airport can be as self-sustaining as possible. This law says an airport owner or operator who renews a covered lease will not be treated as breaking that promise. A covered lease must already exist before the law was enacted, have a nominal rent, have a federal or state government lessee, and support Air Force or Air National Guard aircraft at or from the airport.

who_it_affects.group: Airport owners and operators that hold federal airport improvement grants
who_it_affects.how: They can renew a covered lease without that renewal counting as a violation of the grant assurance on self-sustaining passenger charges.

who_it_affects.group: Federal and state government entities that lease airport space for military aircraft
who_it_affects.how: Covered leases with these government lessees can be renewed under the law's terms.

who_it_affects.group: Air Force and Air National Guard units that operate aircraft at or from covered airports
who_it_affects.how: Their existing low-rent leases at qualifying airports can be renewed under the law's terms.
The law does not change ticket prices or passenger fees directly, but it affects how airports may treat rent from covered leases when setting passenger charges.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The summary does not state a specific effective date; the law was enacted October 7, 2016.
